_comment: Round 09 - FIVE humanoid war mechs that are the SAME MODEL as r04_02 (the attached reference), standing on two legs, in five colourways. Round 07 copied r04_02's PALETTE onto round 06's units. Round 08 copied round 04's STYLE onto generic war mechs. Neither copied the DESIGN. So round 09 transcribes the reference model's actual chassis, feature by feature, and stands it up: the forward-thrusting wedge torso with a heavy chest jutting forward and down, the low wide armoured head with a single wide visor band and cheek tusk spurs, the pair of huge flat dorsal fins sweeping up and out from the shoulders (kept - they are the model's signature - but given a defined construction so they are not random spikes), the row of short cylindrical weapon tubes along the spine, the underslung mechanical pod below the belly, the two heavy digitigrade legs with angular chevron-marked shin plates and broad clawed feet, the right arm ending in a long combat blade described by its parts, and the left arm ending in a three-talon gripping claw. Art style is round 04's styleSuffix, verbatim. The five units are one chassis in five liveries, which is what the brief asked for: 'another set of the same variation of this model'.
_variationAxis: LIVERY only. The chassis, arms, head, fins, spine rack, belly pod and legs are identical on all five units - that is what makes them read as the same model. Only the hues and the placement of the accent colour change.
promptPrefix: A single full-body hero concept-art portrait of a bipedal war machine built on a low forward-thrusting war hound chassis, two legs and two arms, a low wide armoured head thrust forward between the shoulders and
styleSuffix: . Standing on a seamless neutral silver-grey studio backdrop with a soft contact shadow under its feet. The backdrop is plain and empty: no landscape, no sky, no horizon, no ground scenery, no buildings, no props, no weapons on the ground, no rubble. Nothing else in the frame except the machine and its shadow. Brutalist heavy war machine design: massive armoured slabs and thick structural ribs, visible rivets and weld seams, exposed hydraulic actuators and cable looms, armour scorched and battle-damaged with soot streaks, chipped paint showing bare steel, scorch marks and paint burns, dust and grit caked into the lower legs, painted chevron hazard stripes that read as plain geometric shapes and never as characters, and nothing readable on any surface - no letters, no numbers, no words, no signage, no logos. Every machine in this set is the same chassis, built to one identical design standard: the same forward-thrusting wedge torso, a heavy armoured chest that juts forward and down over the hips and tapers back to a narrow spine; the same low wide armoured head with a single wide visor band across the face and a pair of short tusk-like armour spurs at the cheeks; the same pair of large flat dorsal fins sweeping up and outward from the shoulders, each one a broad bevelled plate with a raised central spine ridge, a recessed mounting socket at the base and a squared root fairing where it meets the back plate; the same row of short cylindrical weapon tubes running along the spine behind the head; the same underslung mechanical pod hanging below the centre of the belly with heavy cables running into it; the same two heavy digitigrade legs with large angular shin plates and broad clawed feet, and a pair of painted double chevrons on each shin plate; the same right arm ending in a long straight combat blade, a narrow double-edged taper running the full length of the forearm with a serrated spine along the top edge and a squared grip housing at the base, the blade hanging straight down past the knee and clear of the body; the same left arm ending in a heavy gripping claw, three long curved talons tapering to sharp points; and the same livery structure, one dominant rust and scorched-iron armour colour over a dark charcoal structural colour with a single worn accent colour. Shot identically on every machine: a relaxed upright standing pose with the weight even on both legs and the feet planted slightly apart, the body square and tall, a low three-quarter front view from the left, camera at chest height, a 50mm lens, the whole machine in frame with clear air around it. Heavy military concept art in the same painterly semi-realistic real-robot mecha illustration style as the earlier rounds, smooth airbrushed gradients, soft volumetric haze, gentle film grain, studio key light high above and slightly to the left, falling on the machine only, cool soft fill on the camera-facing side, a bright thin edge highlight running down the left side of the machine, flat even overhead ambient lighting on the floor, the floor a matte plane of one uniform neutral grey with no horizontal gradient across it, all the way to every edge of the frame, with no directional falloff, no pool of light, no bright corner, no dark corner and no reflection. Huge readable silhouette, crisp negative space between the limbs, fine mechanical detail, deep contact shadows. No text, no lettering, no watermark, no scenery, no extra limbs, no duplicated parts.
